section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch6 — Gardner's Multiple Intelligences (Individual Types)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student is highly skilled at sensing classmates' moods, mediating quarrels between friends, and organising group activities that keep everyone included. According to Gardner, this student is strong in:
explanation: Interpersonal intelligence is the capacity to understand and effectively interact with other people — distinct from intrapersonal intelligence (self-understanding).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch6 — Gardner's Multiple Intelligences (Individual Types)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student keeps a personal diary reflecting deeply on their own feelings, sets clear personal goals, and has an accurate sense of their own strengths and weaknesses. According to Gardner, this reflects strength in:
explanation: Intrapersonal intelligence is self-directed — accurate self-knowledge, self-reflection, and understanding one's own emotions and motivations.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch6 — Gardner's Multiple Intelligences (Individual Types)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student learns new dance steps and sports techniques after watching them only once, and communicates ideas effectively through gesture and physical movement in a skit. This is an example of Gardner's:
explanation: Bodily-kinesthetic intelligence is skill in using one's body to solve problems, create products, or express ideas — seen in dancers, athletes, actors, and craftspersons.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch6 — Gardner's Multiple Intelligences (Individual Types)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student can identify a wrong note in a song immediately, easily reproduce rhythms after hearing them once, and remembers lessons better when set to a tune. According to Gardner, this student is strong in:
explanation: Musical intelligence is sensitivity to pitch, rhythm, timbre, and tone.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch6 — Gardner's Multiple Intelligences (Individual Types)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student can mentally rotate a 3-D shape to imagine how it looks from another angle, reads maps easily, and draws accurate, well-proportioned diagrams. According to Gardner, this reflects strength in:
explanation: Spatial intelligence is the capacity to perceive, mentally manipulate, and reproduce visual-spatial relationships.
